question: The earliest ECG change in hyperkalaemia is peaked (tall, narrow, symmetrical) T waves, which can appear when serum potassium exceeds 5.5–6.0 mmol/L.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Peaked T waves are the earliest ECG sign of hyperkalaemia. The progression is: peaked T waves (K⁺ 5.5–6.5) → PR prolongation and P-wave flattening (K⁺ 6.5–7.0) → QRS widening (K⁺ >7.0) → sine-wave pattern → ventricular fibrillation. Never wait for QRS widening before treating.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Peaked T waves are the earliest ECG manifestation of hyperkalaemia, appearing at K⁺ ≈5.5–6.5 mmol/L. With worsening hyperkalaemia, the sequence progresses: peaked T waves → prolonged PR → widened QRS → sine wave → VF/asystole. Treatment must begin before the ECG deteriorates.
